summary: Inference-time LLM optimization can cut API spend by 50-80% without any model retraining, primarily through caching, compression, and smart model routing. Provider prompt caching alone reduces costs 41-80% (per PwC's January 2026 research) while batch APIs deliver an instant 50% discount, and layering exact-match, semantic, and prefix caches can add another 20-40%. The teams that instrument hit rate per cache layer and cap context size are the ones who actually capture these savings.

techniques.name: Provider Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuse the cached KV state of a repeated prompt prefix (system prompts, few-shot examples, long documents) so the provider doesn't re-process those tokens on every call. This is zero correctness risk and should be adopted first.
techniques.savings: 41-80% reduction on cached input tokens; also improves time-to-first-token by 13-31%
techniques.example: Place your large static system prompt and few-shot examples at the start of every request; with Anthropic set a cache_control breakpoint, and OpenAI caches 1024+ token prefixes automatically, so repeated calls bill the prefix at a steep discount.

techniques.name: Batch APIs
techniques.description: Submit non-latency-sensitive requests through asynchronous batch endpoints that return results within a window (typically 24h) in exchange for a flat discount.
techniques.example: Route nightly document-summarization or bulk classification jobs through OpenAI's Batch API instead of synchronous calls to halve the cost with no code logic changes beyond submitting a JSONL file.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Cache responses keyed by embedding similarity rather than exact string match, so queries that mean the same thing return a stored answer and bypass the model entirely. Harder to operate because hits are probabilistic and require false-positive-rate evaluation.
techniques.savings: 20-45% additional reduction on top of provider caching (45% cache hit rates reported in production)
techniques.example: Convert each incoming support query to a vector embedding, search your cache for entries with cosine similarity > 0.85, and if found return the cached answer so 'What's your return policy?' reuses the response generated for 'How do I return a product?'

techniques.name: Exact-Match Caching
techniques.description: Store and instantly return responses for identical queries at sub-millisecond latency, avoiding the LLM inference call entirely for repeated identical requests.
techniques.savings: 100% on cache hits (common in high-repetition chatbots)
techniques.example: Hash the full normalized prompt and store responses in Redis; on an exact hash hit, return the stored completion in sub-millisecond time without calling the model.

techniques.name: Smart Model Routing & Cascading
techniques.description: Route each request to the cheapest model capable of handling its complexity, escalating to larger models only when a cheaper one fails a confidence or validation check.
techniques.savings: 50-90% reduction by sending the majority of traffic to small/cheap models
techniques.example: Classify incoming queries and send simple FAQ-style requests to GPT-4o-mini or an open-weight model while reserving GPT-4-class models for complex reasoning — one reported stack sent 70% of traffic to the cheaper tier.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression (LLMLingua)
techniques.description: Use a compression model like LLMLingua to remove low-information tokens from prompts and long contexts with minimal performance loss, shrinking input token counts.
techniques.savings: 20-30% token reduction (and much higher for verbose contexts)
techniques.example: Pass retrieved RAG chunks through LLMLingua before injecting them into the prompt to cut context tokens ~30% while preserving answer quality.

techniques.name: Context Window & Retrieval Budgeting
techniques.description: Cap the context assembled per request to a fixed token budget, prioritizing the most relevant retrieved chunks over volume, and compress conversation history at phase boundaries.
techniques.savings: 30-60% reduction in input tokens on long-context workloads
techniques.example: In Claude Code, keep your CLAUDE.md rules file under 5,000 tokens and run /compact at natural phase boundaries to compress accumulated conversation context.

techniques.name: Lean Prompt Engineering & Structured Outputs
techniques.description: Trim verbose instructions and use structured outputs / JSON schemas so the model produces compact, parseable responses instead of long prose, reducing both input and expensive output tokens.
techniques.savings: 10-30% reduction, concentrated on costly output tokens
techniques.example: Request a JSON schema with only the fields you need and add 'respond concisely' so the model returns {"intent":"refund","priority":"high"} instead of a paragraph of explanation.

techniques.name: KV Cache Management (self-hosted)
techniques.description: On self-hosted inference servers, apply cache eviction, compression (quantization/pooling), and hybrid CPU/NVMe offloading to serve more concurrent requests per GPU, per a March 2026 Dell survey of techniques.
techniques.savings: Significant throughput/memory gains; no single technique wins alone — combinations work best
techniques.example: Enable prefix-caching plus KV quantization in vLLM so repeated system-prompt tokens are reused and the KV cache fits more sequences in GPU memory.

techniques.name: Open-Weight Model Substitution
techniques.description: Replace commercial API calls with self-hosted or cheap-hosted open-weight models for suitable tasks, eliminating per-token API pricing in favor of fixed infrastructure cost.
techniques.example: Serve a quantized Llama or Qwen model on your own GPUs for high-volume classification, reserving paid APIs only for the hardest requests.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLMs that stores responses by embedding similarity to serve near-duplicate queries without hitting the model.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, self-hosted; infra costs only)

tools.name: Redis (LangCache / Semantic Cache)
tools.description: In-memory data store offering exact-match and vector-based semantic caching with multi-tier strategies and sub-millisecond latency for LLM apps.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; Redis Cloud from ~$5/mo, enterprise/LangCache usage-based pricing

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, model routing/fallbacks, rate limiting, and spend tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/mo for SSO, admin, and support

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and cost-monitoring proxy with request logging, caching, and per-model spend analytics to find and cut waste.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k logs/mo); paid plans from $20/mo, scaling with usage

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with pluggable caching layers (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, GPTCache), prompt management, and model routing abstractions.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LangSmith observability from ~$39/seat/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft's prompt-compression toolkit that shrinks prompts and long contexts with minimal performance loss to reduce input tokens.

tools.name: vCache
tools.description: Semantic cache that returns cached responses for similar prompts under user-defined error-rate guarantees, saving both input and output tokens.

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference server with automatic prefix caching, KV-cache optimization, and quantization for self-hosted open-weight models.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source; GPU infra costs only)

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway providing semantic caching, model routing/fallbacks, cost governance, and observability across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid plans from ~$49/mo plus usage

quick_wins: Enable provider prompt caching and put all static system prompts and few-shot examples at the start of every request for an immediate 40-80% cut on repeated input tokens.
Move all non-latency-sensitive and bulk jobs to the provider Batch API for an instant 50% discount with no logic changes.
Add an exact-match cache (e.g. Redis) in front of your LLM so identical repeated queries return instantly at zero model cost.
Route simple/low-complexity requests to a cheaper model like GPT-4o-mini or an open-weight model via LiteLLM, reserving frontier models for hard tasks.
Trim verbose prompts, cap your context/rules files (e.g. keep CLAUDE.md under 5,000 tokens), and request concise structured JSON outputs to cut both input and output tokens.
